note: Member A candidate, NOT validated. rice_blast: values taken from the cited Government of India (DPPQ&S) advisory and mapped onto the engine's weather variables; the mapping choices (daily mean for the temperature range, hours of RH >= 95% as a proxy for leaf wetness) are listed in Member_A/SOURCES.md. It stays PLACEHOLDER until an agronomist checks the source and the mapping and adds verified_by/verified_on. brown_planthopper: no numeric weather threshold was found in the authoritative sources consulted (DPPQ&S advisory, NIPHM rice IPM package, IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank), so its values are unchanged from the original development placeholder. past_days, forecast_days, full_score_days and min_hours_per_day are engine operating choices, not taken from any source.

pests.name: Rice blast (leaf / neck)

sources.title: Advisory on blast disease (Magnaporthe oryzae) on rice crop, F.No 3-6/2022-23, dated 22.07.2022. Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
sources.note: Quoted: "Rice blast is favored by low temperatures (22-28°C), high relative humidity (>95%), dew deposits, leaf wetness for more than 10 hours, application of high nitrogen and aerobic soils." Mapping: 22-28 °C read as the daily mean; '>95% RH' and 'leaf wetness for more than 10 hours' combined as at least 11 hourly values with RH >= 95% (leaf wetness is not measured; RH near saturation is used as a proxy, which is a modelling assumption, not in the source). Dew deposits, nitrogen and soil are not encoded. National advisory to all States/UTs, not specific to Manipur. Accessed 2026-10-08. Not yet checked by an agronomist.

conditions.label: at least 11 h with relative humidity >= 95%

pests.applicability: Rice (kharif), all growth stages, per the source. National advisory to all States/UTs, not specific to Manipur. Read against one Open-Meteo weather point per monitored area.
pests.limitations: Describes weather that FAVOURS blast; it does not detect blast. Leaf wetness is not measured: hours with RH >= 95% stand in for it (a modelling assumption, not in the source). The 22-28 °C range is read as the daily mean. Dew, nitrogen and soil factors are not encoded. TNAU gives different values (RH 93-99%, night temperature 15-20 °C or < 26 °C). Needs an agronomist's decision before VERIFIED.

pests.name: Brown planthopper
pests.applicability: Rice. Development placeholder only: no source backs these values.
pests.limitations: The values (daily mean 25-32 °C, daily mean RH >= 80%) are unsourced placeholders. The authoritative weather-based BPH rules found (ICAR-NCIPM Technical Bulletin 39, 2016, Table 5) are location-specific (Ludhiana, Chinsurah, Raipur, Hyderabad, Mandya, Aduthurai; none in Manipur), use weekly means, morning/evening RH, sunshine and wind, and count how many of 5-6 criteria are met. The engine's daily all-conditions rule cannot express them, so they were not copied in. Field-scouting thresholds (TNAU ETL, IRRI) are in advisories.md, not here.
